title: Not-Guilty Plea in Rio Bravo Maquinitas Robbery Case
excerpt: Sergio Javier Torres pleaded not guilty Sept. 29 in 341st District Court to robbery and engaging in organized criminal activity charges stemming from a July 9 incident at Las Maquinitas in Rio Bravo, according to the Laredo Morning Times.
content:
Sergio Javier Torres pleaded not guilty on Sept. 29, 2026, in the 341st District Court before Judge Oscar Hale to robbery and engaging in organized criminal activity charges stemming from an incident at Las Maquinitas in Rio Bravo, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

Torres waived the formal reading of the indictment and requested pretrial settings, the newspaper reported. An informal hearing scheduled for Oct. 23 was not held, and the case remains set for pretrial on Dec. 1. The case was filed July 22, 2026.

The robbery charge is a second-degree felony carrying 2 to 20 years in prison, and the engaging in organized criminal activity charge is a state-jail felony carrying 180 days to 2 years in state jail, according to the newspaper.

According to the Webb County Sheriff’s Office, deputies responded on July 9 to an assault at “Las Maquinitas,” in the 1200 block of Espejo Molina in Rio Bravo. A woman said a man went in and forcefully took money from her. Surveillance showed a man wearing a red and black T-shirt with an “American Fighter” logo and blue jeans forcefully taking money from the victim’s hands and running out the back.

Authorities located the suspect at the H-E-B parking lot in the 2300 block of East Saunders Street and identified him as Sergio Javier Torres, the newspaper reported. Sheriff Martin Cuellar thanked the deputies and investigators involved.

Source: Laredo Morning Times, Nov. 14, 2026.
